rules.note: Claim priority is your preference among claims, not your league waiver rank. Successful claims move a team to the back; weekly resets follow league settings. ESPN controls processing time and awards.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ashton Jeanty looked like a franchise back in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, turning 29 touches into 147 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The ankle injury that limited him in training camp and the preseason was no longer an issue, and the second-year RB dominated the workload, as rookie backup Mike Washington notched only seven carries. Jeanty's pass-catching role could be cut back once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to return, but he will remain a focal point of the offense heading into a Week 2 clash with a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ashton Jeanty has looked the part of a bell-cow running back to begin his second NFL season, amassing 54 touches through two games and turning them into 210 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The 2025 first-round pick is still only averaging 3.4 yards per carry however, and the Raiders' offseason upgrades to the offensive line haven't yet led to better efficiency on the ground for Jeanty. He'll try to take advantage of a Week 3 clash with a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ashton Jeanty continues to garner a big workload for the Raiders, but he isn't yet consistently producing big numbers. Through three games, the second-year back is tied for third in the NFL in touches with 76, behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson, but Jeanty's averaging just 3.3 yards per carry and his 303 scrimmage yards are only 14th in the league. He also has yet to score a rushing touchdown in 2026, although he did haul in two TD catches in Week 1. Jeanty will try to improve his efficiency in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ashton Jeanty continues to bolster his lackluster rushing numbers with big production through the air. In the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, the second-year RB managed just 58 rushing yards on 15 carries, but he added six catches for 68 yards on a season-high eight targets. Jeanty's 3.4 yards per carry and zero TDs on the ground through four weeks are a concern, but his 19-165-2 line on 24 targets softens the blow. He'll take on a Patriots defense in Week 5 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ashton Jeanty continues to keep his production afloat via his skills as a pass-catcher. The second-year running back is averaging just 3.3 yards per carry after another poor showing on the ground in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, but he's supplied a 22-215-2 line on 30 targets through five games. The 30 targets are third in the league among RBs, behind the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs and the Rams' Kyren Williams, while Jeanty's receiving yards are third behind Gibbs and the Steelers' Jaylen Warren. Jeanty will try to deliver a more well-rounded line in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and 31st in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ashton Jeanty scored his first rushing touchdown of the season in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, but it was otherwise another lackluster performance for the second-year running back. Jeanty is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry, and the inefficiency is costing him volume, as he hasn't handled 20-plus touches in a game since Week 4. He remains involved as a pass catcher, however, hauling in at least three passes in every game this year while compiling a 26-251-2 line on 36 targets through six contests. Jeanty could contribute through the air in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but 29th in receiving yards per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground while making an impact as a pass catcher. In the Raiders' Week 7 loss to the Rams, the second-year player gained a season-low 15 rushing yards on eight carries, but caught all eight of his targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. Jeanty has gotten at least six targets in six of seven games so far in 2026, turning that volume into a 34-312-3 line on 44 looks. but his 3.1 yards per carry suggests he simply isn't cut out to be a No. 1 back. He'll try to bring some balance to his stat line in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ashton Jeanty is coming off another poor effort, managing just 20 scrimmage yards on 11 touches in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. This time, he wasn't overshadowed by rookie Mike Washington, who lost a total of three yards on his six carries. Jeanty maintains a shaky hold on the top spot in the backfield, but he hasn't reached 30 rushing yards in a game since Week 4, and his contributions of late have been limited to his usage as a pass-catcher. Jeanty isn't likely to turn things around in Week 10 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeanty is eyeing a leap forward in his second NFL season after an uneven rookie campaign in which the first-round pick enjoyed a ton of volume (seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions) and played fairly well (eighth among RBs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF) but struggled to overcome the shaky Las Vegas offense. The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Nabers injured his shoulder last game for the Giants. He was able to return, but still may undergo additional testing this week. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Nabers will likely see his stock take a hit. However, if Nabers can suit up in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Nabers shook off a shoulder injury to suit up last game for the Giants. He responded with five catches on six targets, though racked up a mere 26 yards in the 12-7 win over the Titans. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Nabers. However, Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Nabers exploded last game for 112 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants to victory. Nabers snagged six passes on seven targets for a season-high in terms of receiving yardage. He and quarterback Jameis Winston finally appeared to be on the same page. In Week 5, Nabers and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Malik Nabers saw a staggering 20 targets last game for the Giants. Nabers parlayed those ample opportunities into 11 grabs for 121 yards and a touchdown. It was the second-straight 100-yard outing for Nabers, who also scored for the second-consecutive contest. His newfound connection with starting quarterback Jameis Winston has been evident. In Week 6, the G-Men face a New Orleans defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Saints are allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Nabers continues his torrid stretch for the Giants. Nabers snagged 12 passes for 165 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. Regardless of who has lined up under center for the Giants, Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in three-straight contests. He has racked up a staggering 35 targets in his last two outings alone. In Week 7, Nabers has another favorable matchup against a leaky Texans secondary. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malik Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in four-straight contests for the Giants. Nabers has racked up a staggering 36 catches for 509 yards and two touchdowns over that span. He has drawn an insane 51 targets during that time period, an average of nearly 13 opportunities per clash. In Week 9, the G-Men will face a scuffling Eagles squad. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Malik Nabers had a four-game 100-yard receiving streak snapped last game for the Giants. Nabers had five catches for 43 yards in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. He was targeted eight times. He will look to rebound in Week 10 against a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start needs to be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Allen looks to continue to provide elite returns when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Allen is coming off his best rushing effort of the year in Week 5, finishing with 121 yards while scoring on the ground for the eighth time in five games, adding further upside to his reliable passing efforts. Facing a Raiders defense in Week 6 that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks likely won't hinder Allen's appeal, as he's set for top-tier dual-threat production Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Allen hopes to have his full complement of receivers when the Bills come out of their bye to host the Ravens in Week 8. He failed to record a rushing score in Week 6 for the first time all season, but threw multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 2, maintaining his elite fantasy scoring. This game could bring shootout potential if Baltimore gets Lamar Jackson back under center. Baltimore's defense has been solid against opposing passers, allowing just five touchdown passes in six games before being solved by Joe Burrow for four in Week 7. They've also allowed just one rushing touchdown to the position, but Allen is matchup-proof.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Allen has his work cut out for him when the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9. He ran for his ninth touchdown in seven games during Week 8 and tossed two touchdown passes for the fourth time this season. He's matchup-proof, but Allen will face constant pressure from Minnesota's heavy blitzing scheme that's allowed only four touchdown passes and 81 rushing yards to opposing quarterbacks through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Allen will seek a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. In Week 9 at Minnesota, Allen, in the face of constant pressure, had his first game of the year with just one touchdown while being held under 250 yards for the fourth time. The Jets have allowed a 16:1 TD:INT ratio through nine games, but Allen threw for only 148 yards and no scores against them in his lone 2025 matchup, suggesting a lower-than-usual ceiling for arguably the league's best quarterback.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameson Williams will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Williams found the end zone twice in a Week 5 win over the Cardinals before Detroit's bye week, which was done with two catches for 47 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now totaled 18 grabs for 276 yards and two scores on the season. He'll face a Green Bay secondary that's ranked in the middle versus fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jameson Williams will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Williams produced his best fantasy performance of the year in a Week 7 win over Green Bay, hauling in five of nine targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns. The speedy wideout has now produced four touchdowns in his last two games, along with seven catches for 138 yards in that stretch. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jameson Williams will look to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Williams kept his touchdown streak and recent dominance alive in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, reeling in four of six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown. The speedy wideout has now logged 11 catches for 208 yards and a whopping five touchdowns in his last three outings. He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jameson Williams will look to get more volume as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Williams struggled to get touches with a stagnant passing game against the Dolphins in Week 9, recording one catch for 31 yards and one rush for nine yards. The speedy wideout has now posted a 28-468-5 receiving line on 44 targets across eight games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Kittle could again be a key component of San Francisco's offense in Week 5 against Seattle. Kittle has scored a touchdown in three straight games, and he got into the end zone on a game-sealing 56-yard reception in Week 4 versus the Broncos. The veteran tight end enters the clash against Seattle with 244 receiving yards on the season, third-most among NFL tight ends. With that said, the Seahawks' defense has given up the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends, so Kittle has his work cut out for him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Kittle should be past an illness by the time the 49ers face Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 6. Kittle suited up this past Sunday against Seattle despite falling under the weather near game day. He ended up with a modest five catches on six targets for 24 yards but logged his usual big workload with a season-high 93 percent offensive snap share. Kittle could be primed for a big game against the Commanders, who have surrendered 15.8 fantasy points per game -- second-most in the league -- to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Kittle and the 49ers are in Atlanta as they look to stay undefeated in Week 7. He caught five of eight targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during San Francisco's 23-17 win in Week 6. Kittle finished second on the team in receptions, yardage and targets on a night where Brock Purdy attempted just 29 passes. The talented tight end boasts a 26-337-5 line on 36 targets through six outings, and he'll aim to keep rolling versus a Falcons defense tied for 23rd in fantasy points allowed per game (16.0) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 9 matchup versus the Raiders well-rested following his team's Week 8 bye. Kittle had his snaps managed each of the first two weeks following his January surgery to repair a torn Achilles tendon, but amid multiple injuries to the 49ers' WR corps, the star tight end logged at least an 85% offensive snap share (and at least six targets) in each of his past five games. San Francisco could get multiple of the injured wideouts back for Week 9, but Kittle should still be a big part of the passing game, as he ranks fifth among NFL tight ends with a 22.4% target share this season. He'll face a Las Vegas defense that has given up eight touchdowns to tight ends, tied for second-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: George Kittle's health and productivity have been huge this season for the 49ers heading into a Week 10 tilt against Dallas. After undergoing surgery in January to repair a torn Achilles, Kittle has played in every one of San Francisco's games this season and leads the club with 38 receptions, 483 receiving yards and five receiving touchdowns. His role in the passing game has been especially important of late, as Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) have been sidelined due to injuries, and the addition of veteran possession receiver Keenan Allen at the trade deadline isn't likely to impact Kittle's routes down the seams. Kittle will look to find success against a Dallas defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against tight ends, yielding 7.7 fantasy points per game to the position (tied for 12th in the league).

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wan'Dale Robinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans, but he's averaging just 31 receiving yards per game as a Titan after coming over from the Giants in free agency. Houston has been surprisingly poor at defending wide receivers, allowing the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and TDs (six) to the position. Robinson's inconsistent usage in a low-octane passing game makes him hard to trust, but he's a viable flex option for Week 5 given the Texans' struggles against his position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wan'Dale Robinson is averaging just 35 receiving yards per game for the Titans heading into a Week 6 road affair against the Colts, who are allowing 160 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Robinson has drawn at least five targets from Cam Ward in all but one game this season, and his steady involvement makes him a viable flex play for Week 6 against the Colts' beatable pass defense. However, Robinson's ceiling is capped due to the poor play of Tennessee's entire offense, which ranks last leaguewide with 11.6 points per game. Two of Ward's three touchdown passes through five games have gone to Robinson.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wan'Dale Robinson drew 30 targets from Titans QB Cam Ward over the past four games. Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll loved peppering Robinson with short targets when they were together on the Giants, and Daboll has maintained that philosophy in their new surroundings. Robinson has caught 19 of those 30 targets for 151 yards and two TDs, and his consistent involvement in Tennessee's offense gives him a respectable floor as a solid Week 7 flex option against the Browns, who are giving up 157 yards per game to WRs and have allowed seven TDs to the position through six games. Robinson and QB Cam Ward are the only Titans with multiple TDs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Wan'Dale Robinson mustered just seven yards on four catches in the Titans' Week 7 loss to the Browns, and he's likely to continue earning a steady diet of short passes from Cam Ward in Week 8 against the Bengals. Robinson has 23 catches over the past five games but is averaging a career-low 7.1 yards per reception in his fifth NFL season and first with Tennessee. He's a high-floor, low-ceiling flex option for Week 8 against the Bengals, who are allowing 138 yards per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Wan'Dale Robinson should have enough short passes thrown his way to maintain flex appeal for Tennessee's Week 10 home game against the Jaguars. The 1-7 Titans are likely to fall behind against the 6-2 Jaguars and throw plenty against a Jacksonville secondary that's allowing 175 yards per game to WRs. Robinson has caught three of Cam Ward's six touchdown passes this season and has drawn at least six targets in four consecutive games, though the former Giants WR hasn't exceeded 57 yards in a Titans jersey.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tony Pollard is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game and scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Ravens, though that wasn't enough to keep the Titans from dropping to 0-4. In Week 5, Tennessee hosts the AFC South rival Texans, who are also 0-4. The Titans should manage to stay within striking distance and give Pollard his full workload on the ground, though Houston has held RBs to just 91 scrimmage yards per game. Pollard is a high-floor, low-ceiling flex play as usual for Week 5 given his role as the lead back in a struggling Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards and second-fewest points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tony Pollard remains a viable flex option in Week 6 against the Colts thanks to his high touch floor as the starting RB in a putrid Titans offense. Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season but has been limited to one TD on a Titans offense that has found the end zone just six times through five games. Indianapolis is giving up 100 rushing yards per game to RBs as well as a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to the position, so Pollard has a higher ceiling than usual in this Week 6 matchup to go with his steady floor.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tony Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in each of the Titans' last five games. He's locked into a high touch floor in any game the 1-5 Titans can keep within striking distance, and Tennessee is unlikely to fall too far behind in Week 7 at home against the Browns, who are scoring just 17.7 points per game, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL. Cleveland has started 4-2 thanks to a stout defense that's allowing 20.3 points per game and has allowed just one TD to a running back all season, but Pollard's hefty usage keeps him locked in as a viable flex play for Week 7, even though he looks unlikely to add to his season total of one TD in a Titans offense that's tied for the worst in the league at 14.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tony Pollard is coming off his best game of the season, as he racked up 129 rushing yards and three TDs against the Browns in Tennessee's Week 7 loss. The veteran RB is the most consistent offensive player on the Titans, having racked up at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in six consecutive games. His solid touch floor makes Pollard a passable fantasy RB2 for Week 8, but don't expect a repeat of his Week 7 outburst against a Bengals defense that has limited RBs to three total TDs in six games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tony Pollard delivered consecutive elite performances prior to Tennessee's Week 9 bye, racking up 292 scrimmage yards and five TDs across losses to the Browns and Bengals. Prior to that two-game stretch, he had just one TD through seven games and no 100-yard performances. If he isn't traded prior to Tuesday's deadline, Pollard would maintain fantasy RB2 upside for Week 10 despite a difficult matchup against a Jaguars defense that's holding RBs to 68 yards per game. Even before his recent uptick in production, Pollard had a solid floor as the clear lead back for Tennessee.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season. However, he was overshadowed by Bucky Irving in Week 1, who caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards, while Gainwell was targeted just once. He will likely need more receiving work to be fantasy relevant in a Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed just two receptions for 22 yards to RBs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Gainwell is likely to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Gainwell has logged just 10 rush attempts for 21 yards through three games this season, confirming he's firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. The first-year Buccaneer has yet to score a touchdown as well, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a score. Despite this, Gainwell is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Packers defense that's already given up six rushing touchdowns this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Gainwell found the end zone for the first time this season during the Week 4 loss to the Packers. However, he remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield, as Irving out-touched Gainwell 16 to five. Gainwell will likely struggle maintaining fantasy relevance in Week 5 without scoring another touchdown, though the Cowboys defense has already allowed four rushing TDs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Gainwell has operated as Tampa Bay's top receiving back over the last two weeks, getting more targets (six), receptions (five) and yards (32) than Bucky Irving (two catches on three targets for 10 yards). Despite this, Gainwell will likely struggle finding fantasy relevance without scoring a touchdown. He could thrive against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed 200 receiving yards to RBs through five contests, tied for the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Gainwell was given few opportunities in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, accumulating 24 total yards on just three touches. Additionally, Gainwell was on the field for just 15% of Tampa Bay's offensive plays, his lowest mark of the season. It appears as if Gainwell is trending toward receiving less work as the season progresses, but he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Panthers defense that's allowed 5.1 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Gainwell had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing 14 times for 88 yards. Despite his productive day, Gainwell still tallied 10 fewer carries than Bucky Irving (24 rushes for 106 yards and two touchdowns), suggesting he remains firmly behind Irving in Tampa Bay's backfield. However, Gainwell could remain successful in Week 8 against a Falcons defense that's given up 10 total touchdowns to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kenny Gainwell will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He racked up a career-high 140 rushing yards on 25 carries in the Week 8 win over the Falcons, bringing his season total to 289 yards (5.0 yards per carry). Despite Gainwell's huge performance, he still remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. Gainwell could struggle, especially against a strong Bears defense that has allowed just three rushing touchdowns to RBs all season.

player.seasonOutlook: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: RJ Harvey is coming off the best performance of his career as a pass catcher, posting a 10-68-0 line on 10 targets while adding 25 rushing yards on seven carries in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. Denver trailed most of the game, which helped boost the second-year back's usage, but J.K. Dobbins' struggles in the early-down role are also opening the door for Harvey to log more touches in general, as his seven carries were also a season high. The eventual return of rookie Jonah Coleman from a high-ankle sprain could shake up the backfield further, but until then Harvey's arrow appears to be pointed up. He'll look to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs..
outlooksByWeek.6: RJ Harvey all but vanished from the Broncos' game plan in Week 5, gaining seven yards on three carries and failing to catch his only target as Sean Payton returned to play-calling duties. His usage as a pass-catcher was especially disappointing after the second-year back was fed 17 targets over the prior two weeks, turning that volume into a 16-109-0 line. J.K. Dobbins is the preferred early-down option in the backfield, and Harvey's value could become very dependent on game flow as a result. He might see more work in Week 6 if Denver falls behind early against a Seattle team that's in the bottom seven in the league in receptions per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: RJ Harvey found the end zone for the first time in 2026 during the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The second-year running back managed just 56 scrimmage yards on nine touches as he continues to work behind J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. Harvey's target volume has declined since Sean Payton took back play-calling duties, notching only five targets the last two weeks while producing a 3-31-0 line through the air. Harvey will try to reclaim a more consistent role in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: RJ Harvey logged just five touches in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, but he turned one of them into a 52-yard TD reception in the third quarter to salvage his day. The second-year back finished third in the backfield in workload behind rookie Jonah Coleman (11 touches) and veteran J.K. Dobbins (six touches), but Harvey seems to have a steady role as a passing-down option for Bo Nix. Even if Sean Payton continues to roll with a committee approach to his ground game, Harvey's floor should be relatively secure, even if his ceiling is limited to occasional big plays. He's unlikely to make a splash in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyjae Spears had five touches to Tony Pollard's eight in Tennessee's season-opening loss. Heading into a Week 2 home game against the Eagles, the Titans once again look like one of the NFL's worst offenses. Given Spears' role as a supporting piece in Tennessee's low-octane offense, he's tough to trust as anything more than a low-end deep-league flex play. Spears has exceeded 50 scrimmage yards three times in 14 appearances since the start of last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyjae Spears is likely to see a handful of touches as usual for the Titans behind Tony Pollard in Week 3, but that projected usage is enough for Spears to earn flex consideration in deeper formats against a Giants defense that has struggled to defend RBs. The Giants just allowed at least 92 scrimmage yards apiece to the Rams' backfield duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, but the Rams boast one of the league's most talented offenses and led the league with 30.5 points per game last season, while the Titans are averaging 15.0 PPG after scoring 16.7 PPG last season. Spears can make big plays happen in space, as he showed in compiling 70 yards on nine touches in last week's loss to the Eagles, though he had just 24 yards on five touches in the season-opening loss to the Jets.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyjae Spears was limited to three touches for the Titans in Week 3 while playing through an ankle injury. Even if he heals up ahead of a Week 4 trip to Baltimore, Spears is unlikely to crack double-digits in touches while filling his customary change-of-pace role behind Tony Pollard. The Ravens have been middling against the run but have limited RBs to just 12 receiving yards per game, so Spears is unlikely to earn much Week 4 fantasy lineup consideration outside of super-deep formats.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyjae Spears has been limited to three touches in each of Tennessee's Week 3 and Week 4 games while playing through an ankle injury. Typically, his total is in the high single digits, but Spears' injury concerns, coupled with Tennessee's struggles on offense (13.8 points per game), make the change-of-pace RB a fantasy non-factor ahead of a Week 5 home game against the Texans, who are allowing just 3.5 yards per carry. Tony Pollard should continue to get the majority of opportunities in Tennessee's backfield.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyjae Spears had a season-high 11 touches, including nine catches, in Tennessee's Week 5 loss to the Texans. His contributions as a receiver give Spears some deep-league flex appeal for Week 6 against a Colts defense that's allowing a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to running backs. Tony Pollard remains the top backfield option in a low-octane Titans offense that's scoring a league-low 11.6 points per game, while Spears has only one game with more than 28 scrimmage yards this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyjae Spears exceeded three touches in only one of the Titans' last four games while playing through ankle and knee injuries. He can be an effective pass-catcher out of the backfield when at full strength while spelling starter Tony Pollard, but Spears hasn't provided much production while banged up. Another quiet performance from Spears is likely forthcoming in Week 7 against a Browns defense that has allowed just one TD to running backs all season, so he isn't a recommended fantasy play, even in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyjae Spears has been banged up for most of the season. He sat out Tennessee's Week 7 loss to the Browns due to a knee injury after previously playing through ankle and knee injuries. He's a shifty change-of-pace option when healthy, but Spears won't be an advisable Week 8 fantasy play even if he suits up against the Bengals. Tony Pollard has strengthened his hold on the top spot on Tennessee's RB depth chart with strong play in recent weeks, and Spears is unlikely to score his first TD of the season against a Bengals defense that has allowed just three TDs to RBs through six games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyjae Spears hasn't suited up since Week 6 due to a knee injury and has also dealt with an ankle injury this season. Even if he returns to his customary change-of-pace role for the Titans in Week 10, Spears is unlikely to contribute much against a Jacksonville defense that has been elite at containing RBs. If the Titans trade lead back Tony Pollard, Spears could see an uptick in work, but the biggest beneficiary in that scenario would likely be rookie fifth-round pick Nicholas Singleton.

player.seasonOutlook: Spears is set for his fourth NFL season, including his third as a change-of-pace backup to Tony Pollard. The role hasn't been particularly fruitful from a fantasy standpoint, as Spears has yet to clear five touchdowns in a season, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. Spears, who has also struggled with durability (nine games missed over the past two years), isn't used much as a rusher (100 or fewer carries all three seasons), but he is an effective receiver (top 10 among RBs in catches in both 2023 and 2025). The 25-year-old will resume his role as a receiving specialist in 2026 and, even if the Titans' offense makes a big leap in QB Cam Ward's second season, Spears is unlikely to find his way to consistent fantasy value.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashid Shaheed has yet to make a big impact in fantasy this season with Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers coming up. Though Shaheed has been valuable as a return man for the Seahawks, he's averaging just two catches for 17.7 yards through three weeks. Shaheed also fell below a 50% offensive snap share in Week 3 against Washington, as Cooper Kupp served as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Shaheed may need a big play or two to break out against the Chargers, who have allowed nine receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for 13th-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rashid Shaheed should continue to operate in a versatile role for Seattle in a big Week 5 battle against San Francisco. Though Shaheed had just one catch for 20 yards versus the Chargers in Week 4, he added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown while also returning kickoffs and punts. The 49ers have a similarly versatile player in Deebo Samuel, and the pair of Swiss-army-knife wideouts could be keys in what figures to be a battle of tough defenses. San Francisco has allowed just 17.0 fantasy points per game to WRs this season, sixth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashid Shaheed has been a relatively quiet contributor to Seattle's passing game heading into a Week 6 tilt in Denver. Shaheed has caught three or fewer passes in all of the Seahawks' games so far this season and has yet to record a receiving touchdown, though he does have rushing score on his ledger. The speedy wideout has a big role as an electric kick returner, but Shaheed may struggle to produce as a pass catcher as long as Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to eat up targets. The Broncos are giving up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (16.3) to wideouts this season, but they could be without both starting cornerbacks -- Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) -- in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashid Shaheed and the Seahawks look to snap a two-game losing streak in Week 7 when the Chiefs pay a visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught five of eight targets for 66 yards while rushing once for two yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6. Shaheed also compiled 77 yards on three kickoff returns and another 39 yards on three punt returns, but he fumbled twice while only losing one. He finished second on the Seahawks in yardage, tied with Cooper Kupp for second in receptions, and was third in targets. Shaheed will look to build on that performance versus Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashid Shaheed isn't certain to suit up for Seattle in Week 8 against the Bears. Shaheed injured his knee in Week 7 versus Kansas City, and though initial reports on the injury were promising, it's not clear if he'll need to miss time. The versatile wideout has been pretty quiet as a receiver throughout the campaign, surpassing three receptions just once through seven weeks. That makes him relatively dependent on big plays, and Chicago has given up nine receptions of 40-plus yards this season, most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rashid Shaheed will look to return from a knee injury in time to suit up for Seattle's Week 9 battle against Arizona. Shaheed missed the Week 8 loss to Chicago due to the injury, and it's unclear how close he is to returning to action. Should he be able to return to face the Cardinals, he'll have a good opportunity for success against a suspect Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals have given up 25 receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rashid Shaheed (knee) has missed Seattle's past two games and isn't certain to return in Week 10 against the Raiders. Shaheed hasn't practiced since getting hurt in Week 7, and he'll likely need to return to at least a few limited sessions before being ready to play in games again. Should Shaheed sit out another contest, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton will likely continue to be the Seahawks' top wideouts behind superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If Shaheed can suit up, though, he'll face a Raiders defense that has allowed 27 passing plays of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town for a Week 5 home tilt. He played 75% of snaps on offense and caught three of five targets for 17 yards and his second touchdown of the season. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington (3-27-1) was slightly more productive while playing 70% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like it'll be a toss-up between the two on any given week as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 6. He played 38 snaps on offense (70%) and was highly productive, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two of Aaron Rodgers' three TD passes during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Freiermuth finished third on the team in receptions and yardage, while his seven looks were the second-most. Fellow starting tight end Darnell Washington was on the field for 34 offensive snaps (63%) and caught two of three targets for 12 yards. Freiermuth recorded a second consecutive outing with a score and now has four TDs on the season, and he'll aim to take advantage of a Tampa Bay defense allowing 15.7 fantasy points per game (22nd) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Paris to take on the Saints in Week 7. He caught two of three targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime in Week 6. Freiermuth and fellow tight end Darnell Washington each played 71% of snaps on offense, but it was the latter who made the bigger impact in this one, as Washington tallied a 4-25-1 line on six targets. Freiermuth will try to rebound versus a New Orleans defense that just surrendered six receptions for 99 yards and a TD to Isaiah Likely.
outlooksByWeek.8: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers return home to host the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He caught two of four targets for 20 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 win in Paris. Freiermuth played 34 offensive snaps to fellow TE Darnell Washington's 36, but the two have been essentially neck-and-neck in playing time through seven outings this season. Freiermuth will aim to stand out versus Cleveland's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (13.9) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.10: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Cincinnati for an AFC North showdown in Week 10. He caught both of his targets for 35 yards and rushed once for a one-yard touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 8 victory. Freiermuth finished second on the team in yardage and accounted for one of three rushing TDs despite playing only 53% of the offensive snaps. Over his last three contests, he strung together a 6-66-0 receiving line on nine targets to go along with his one-yard TD run, securing two receptions in each outing. Freiermuth could struggle to hit paydirt for the sixth time this season in a matchup versus a Bengals defense that's given up only one score to opposing TEs through eight games.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Colts in a battle between 2-2 teams in Week 5. He missed his second consecutive game with a toe injury sustained in Week 2. Jaylen Warren accounted for 20 of 22 touches by running backs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, a pattern that would surely continue if Dowdle remains sidelined against Indianapolis. Monitor his practice participation leading up to a favorable matchup versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (24.2) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to face off with the Buccaneers in Week 6. After sitting out the last three games with a toe injury, it appears Dowdle is ready to make his return against the 1-4 Bucs. He was brought to Pittsburgh to form a dynamic one-two punch alongside Jaylen Warren, but the incumbent starter has excelled as the featured player out of the backfield, particularly over the last three weeks. Assuming Dowdle takes the field in Week 6, he's likely to work as the clear backup to Warren, so it's best he remains on fantasy benches versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to Paris for a Week 7 meeting with the Saints. He returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury and registered seven carries for 40 yards and three catches on four targets for nine yards during Pittsburgh's overtime win in Week 6. Dowdle played just 28% of snaps on offense as he works his way back into game shape, and he was pretty effective in limited action, so his workload should rise steadily in Week 7. Jaylen Warren started and earned 16 touches to Dowdle's 10, and there's a good chance they'll both be heavily involved versus a New Orleans defense that ranks dead-last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers look to even the season series against the Browns in Week 8. He rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught all six of his targets for 45 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Paris. Dowdle finished first in receptions and second in yardage despite being out-touched by starter Jaylen Warren, who turned his 21 touches into 137 scrimmage yards. Dowdle was inactive for the Week 4 loss against Cleveland, so he'll look to make an impact with first place in the AFC North at stake.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to take on the Bengals for a Week 10 AFC North showdown. He had his best showing of the season during Week 8's victory, rushing 15 times for 56 yards and his first touchdown with Pittsburgh. Dowdle battled a toe injury in the early portion of the season, but he's starting to come along, tallying 15 touches in each of his previous two outings. He will look to keep improving versus Cincinnati's 15th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (20.9) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

While the Saints showed improvement under first-year defensive coordinator Brandon Staley over the course of 2025 -- their 66 fantasy points following their Week 11 bye was fifth-best in the league -- the team has a rough go of it at the onset of 2026. Road matchups with the Lions (Week 1) and Ravens (2) are tough as nails, and even the addition of LB Kaden Ellis isn't going to ease those matchup worries. Consider this a streaming defense at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Stevens missed a field goal and an extra point in Week 1 for Washington. The Commanders lost by two points, making the misses all the more glaring. Stevens will have a chance to rebound in Week 2, though, as Washington faces a Dallas squad that allowed the most points in the NFL last season, and looked no better in their season opener versus the Giants. Dallas lost an ugly 28-20 affair to the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Stevens missed his second field goal of the season last game for Washington. Stevens did make two other field goals as well as both of his PATs, but the Commanders offense is not a pretty option for a fairly shaky kicker heading into a brutal Week 3 matchup versus Seattle. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per contest thus far this season, which is second in the NFL. In addition, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels is unlikely to play for the Commanders after dislocating his elbow.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drew Stevens connected on an impressive 57-yard field goal in Washington's 33-31 win over the Seahawks last game. However, Stevens also missed an extra point, and has now missed four kicks through three outings. Stevens has a big leg but could be on thin ice with a few more misses. He should have ample opportunities in Week 4 versus the Colts, though. Indianapolis is allowing 30.3 points per tilt, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drew Stevens has made at least two field goals in three-straight games for the Commanders. Stevens connected on two field goals, as well as an extra point, in Washington's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London. In Week 5, Washington will face the first-place New York Giants. New York's defense has been much-improved in 2026, allowing just 19.8 points per tilt, which is eighth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drew Stevens missed an extra point last game for Washington. With the contest resulting in a 27-27 tie, Stevens could have been viewed as the goat. However, late-game clock mismanagement by the offense failed to allow Stevens a chance at redemption, as the Commanders could not get off a game-winning field goal attempt as time expired in overtime. Stevens did hit two other field goals as well as another extra point in the contest. His job should still be safe heading into Week 6 versus the 49ers. However, his opportunities could be limited, as San Fran is yielding just 18.6 points per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drew Stevens has made at least two field goals in four of six games this season for Washington. However, he has made just 10 field goals the entire year overall, while missing three extra points. In Week 8, the Commanders face the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per contest, which is 17th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Drew Stevens connected on two field goals as well as an extra point last game for the Commanders. Stevens has connected on multiple field goals in six of the last seven outings for Washington.  He has six made field goals in his last two games alone. In Week 10, Stevens will take on a Giants squad allowing 21.5 points per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL.
